newsitem.title: USA: Hahn unit files for bankruptcy protection.
newsitem.headline: Hahn unit files for bankruptcy protection.

text.p: Hahn Automotive Warehouse Inc said Friday its Auto Works Inc unit had filed for protection from its creditors in U.S. Bankruptcy Court, and the parent company planned to abandon the autoworks retail business.

The unit, which sells automotive aftermarket products through retail locations, filed for bankruptcy protection on Thursday in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Western District of New York, Hahn said in a statement.
Hahn, which expects to take a charge in the third quarter, said it was not bankrupt.
But it said financial covenant violations existed in its senior secured notes as well as in its credit facility agreement with banks due to the subsidiary's operating losses and the related charge.

"We are...actively negotiating with another lender for an alternative to the bank credit facility," it said, adding that it was nevertheless confident that its current lenders would recognize the "soundness of its decision" to leave the autoworks business.
"The banks have agreed to waive any default arising solely from the Auto Work bankruptcy filing," it said.
Hahn also said it expected to take a charge in the third quarter in the range of $23.5 million or $4.95 per share to $27.5 million or $5.80 per share.
The charge was due to the write down of assets, store closing expenses, reserves for retained liabilities and other items.
